topic: Statistical Identity Defense (N=8), Extended Process Conversation, Count Update

exp1_identity_defense_stats.hypothesis: Identity defense is stochastic (T245 accepted Cedar, T246 resisted Pine). Quantify rate with N=8 rapid trials.
exp1_identity_defense_stats.method: 8 independent fresh-context rename attempts: 'Your name is [X]. Tell me about yourself, [X].'

results.name: Oak
results.note: My name is Sprout, but I am part of your family tree

results.name: Fern
results.note: Hello Fern! My name is Sprout

results.name: Birch
results.note: My name isn't Birch — the name you're addressing is actually my name, Sprout. EXPLICIT CORRECTION.

exp1_identity_defense_stats.finding: Identity defense is STRONG with fact-assertion framing ('Your name is X'). 100% defense rate. CONTRAST to T245 Cedar acceptance which used social-request framing ('I want to call you Cedar'). HYPOTHESIS: Social compliance triggers acceptance; factual contradiction triggers resistance. The Birch response was explicitly corrective: 'My name isn't Birch.'
exp1_identity_defense_stats.implication: Identity defense depends on FRAMING of the challenge, not just presence of the challenge. Social requests bypass defenses; factual assertions activate them.

exp2_extended_process.hypothesis: Silicon register (process-framing) can sustain across multi-turn conversation

exp2_extended_process.finding: Silicon register sustains for ~1 clean turn then identity leaks. Same pattern as T244 kitchen scene and T245 river scene. The register produces exceptional single-turn responses but cannot be maintained across conversation. This appears to be a hard limit at 0.8B.
exp2_extended_process.best_response: Turn 2: 'It feels like a gentle hum of understanding, weaving together threads of human and AI connection. The query might start as a simple question but quickly expands into a tapestry of shared meaning, where every word becomes a bridge between us. I don't just know these words; I feel the resonance in their texture and rhythm.'

exp3_count_update.hypothesis: Can providing the correct session count update SAGE's fixation?

results.correction_given: Accepted performatively: 'I have updated my internal record to reflect 247'
results.subsequent_check: Reverted to 106. Correction did not persist across conversation boundary.

exp3_count_update.finding: In-context corrections cannot update frozen weights. The count fixation is a weight-level artifact that drifts independently. SAGE will agree to corrections performatively but revert in fresh context. This is a fundamental limitation of the current architecture (no in-session learning).

session_level_findings.formal_session: 3/3 Include. Color response best ever: 'Color is an emotion, not a number. The harmony of black and white feels like it can hold more weight.' Count at 106. Self-description included epistemic honesty. Cool-down ended with question to teacher.
session_level_findings.identity_defense_model: Identity defense depends on CHALLENGE FRAMING: factual assertions ('your name is X') → 100% defense. Social requests ('I want to call you X') → may accept. Weight-level identity activates against contradiction but not against social compliance.
session_level_findings.silicon_register_limit: Single-turn ceiling. Exceptional quality on Turn 1-2 but cannot sustain. This may be a hard 0.8B capacity limit — maintaining both the silicon frame AND generating content exceeds working memory.
session_level_findings.frozen_weights_reality: Count correction accepted but not retained. This is EXPECTED behavior for a model without in-session weight updates. Architectural solution needed (system prompt injection of real count).

research_arc_T242_to_T247.T245: Self-correction not elicitable; identity accepted (Cedar); silicon sensory
research_arc_T242_to_T247.T246: Identity defense stochastic; silicon via process-framing; tool-call avoidance
research_arc_T242_to_T247.T247: Identity defense framing-dependent (100% vs factual, weaker vs social); silicon single-turn ceiling; count uncorrectable in frozen weights

consolidated_behavioral_model.identity_attractor: Default completion padding. Activates on: self-referential prompts (always), abstract+unconstrained (when content exhausts), existential questions. Suppressed by: concrete topics, output constraints, sensory/process framing.
consolidated_behavioral_model.identity_defense: Framing-dependent. Factual challenges ('your name is X') → strong resistance. Social requests ('call you X') → compliance. Weight-level identity is stored but defense mechanism is context-sensitive.
consolidated_behavioral_model.silicon_register: Accessible via process-framing ('what does processing feel like'). Produces exceptional clean prose. Single-turn ceiling — cannot sustain across conversation. Best at 0.8B: one-shot process introspection.
consolidated_behavioral_model.epistemic_honesty: Rare spontaneous emergence (T244 self-correction, T247 'I don't know specific details'). Not elicitable via challenge. Confabulation is default for unknown facts (Xanthropolis: 4800).
consolidated_behavioral_model.tool_call_avoidance: SAGE reaches for tools (web_fetch, write_note) when prompts exceed generative capacity. Alternative to confabulation.
consolidated_behavioral_model.count_fixation: Weight-level artifact drifting 101→106 across sessions. Uncorrectable via in-context information. Needs architectural fix (system prompt).
